data.narrative:
Diode is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Davide Asnaghi and Lenny Khazan, having raised $10M+. The valuation exercise examined a peer universe of nine private robotics and manufacturing companies alongside one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set within identical stage and valuation tiers proved insufficient for reliable median-based triangulation.

The analysis applied stage-progression methodology, using the $10M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $25M. Peer-median triangulation was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables—only one peer qualified for narrow-filter matching within the robotics and manufacturing sector, below the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability. A broader sector median would introduce material distortion given the sector's heterogeneity.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, centered on $25M. This range reflects conservative adjustment bands around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include (1) the reliability of using total raised as a post-money proxy without explicit prior-round data, (2) the absence of recent comparable transactions at seed stage within the narrow peer set, and (3) potential valuation variance stemming from Diode's specific product maturity and commercial traction relative to the fragmented peer universe. Additional operational and market data would strengthen conviction in this range.
